fail_intro: As the trail got steeper, the reality of your planning set in.
pass_body: The sun sets behind the ridge as you reach your final camp. Because you packed well, your energy levels stayed high throughout the climb. You successfully completed the trek and learned how your body handles the trail!

failure_scenarios.starving: Without enough calories, your muscles began to fatigue halfway through the distance.
failure_scenarios.dehydrated: Severe dehydration left you feeling lightheaded and unable to focus on the terrain.
failure_scenarios.missing_gear: Missing critical safety gear forced you to turn back before things got dangerous.
failure_scenarios.missing_essentials: Lacking one of the 10 Essentials meant you weren't prepared for the changing conditions.
failure_scenarios.too_heavy: The excessive weight of your pack made every step a struggle, quickly draining your reserves.
failure_scenarios.too_bulky: Your pack was overflowing! You couldn't zip it shut or carry it properly on the trail.
failure_scenarios.lnt_violation: You realized you had no way to pack out your trash, forcing you to abandon the trip to avoid littering.
failure_scenarios.high_caffeine: Jitters from excessive caffeine made your pace erratic and your heart race.
failure_scenarios.high_sugar: A sugar crash left you feeling shaky and weak after an initial energy spike.
failure_scenarios.alcohol_penalty: The alcohol you packed slowed your recovery and significantly dehydrated your system.

weather.HOT: Beat the heat! Make sure to pack extra water and sun protection.
weather.COLD: It's going to be chilly. Don't forget wool layers to stay warm.
weather.RAINY: Rain is in the forecast. A good rain jacket is essential to stay dry.
weather.SNOW: Snowy conditions await. Pack high-calorie food and thermal protection.
weather.WINDY: It's going to be windy. A windbreaker or shell will help you retain heat.

item_weather.HOT: Gear Check: A Hat and Sunscreen are critical. Avoid Cotton Shirts, which trap sweat.
item_weather.COLD: Gear Check: Pack a Wool Shirt for insulation. Avoid Cotton Shirts, which lose all warmth when wet.
item_weather.RAINY: Gear Check: A Rain Jacket is non-negotiable. Consider Ziploc Bags to keep your matches dry.
item_weather.SNOW: Gear Check: Wool Shirts and a Rain Jacket (for snow melt) are required. Don't forget Sunscreen, since snow reflects UV rays!
item_weather.WINDY: Gear Check: A Rain Jacket can double as a windbreaker. A Hat will help retain body heat.

terrain.ROCKY: This rocky terrain can be tough on your joints. Trekking poles are highly recommended.
terrain.DESERT: Desert environments are dry. Prioritize hydration above all else.
terrain.MOUNTAIN: Mountain climbs require serious energy. Bring snacks with a good mix of carbs and protein.
terrain.FOREST: Forest trails are beautiful but can have wildlife. Carry safety gear like a whistle or bear spray.

item_terrain.ROCKY: Gear Check: Trekking Poles will save your knees on the steep rocky descents.
item_terrain.DESERT: Gear Check: Bring a Water Filter if a water source exists, but expect to carry multiple Water Bottles.
item_terrain.MOUNTAIN: Gear Check: Trekking Poles help with elevation gain. A Compass is vital if you lose the trail above the tree line.
item_terrain.FOREST: Gear Check: Bear Spray is essential in dense woods. A Compass will help you navigate if the canopy blocks your view.

adventure.OVERNIGHT: Since you'll be out overnight, shelter and a sleeping bag are mandatory.

item_adventure.OVERNIGHT: Gear Check: A Sleeping Bag, Tent, and Flashlight are mandatory for surviving the night.

duration.LONG: This is a long haul. Be mindful of pack weight, every ounce counts!
